articles.title: India to probe attack on flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar: NIA files case under anti-hijacking law & UAPA
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered a case to investigate the September 30 attack on Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has registered a case to investigate the September 30 attack on Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit of a flydubai flight, officials said on Saturday.The case was registered on October 9 under relevant provisions of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016, and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967, according to officials quoted by PTI.Machchhar was stabbed and seriously injured by his co-pilot inside the cockpit of flydubai flight FZ1073 while the aircraft was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, officials said, citing the FIR. The attack was allegedly carried out in an attempt to hijack the aircraft or cause it to crash.Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing others to overpower the attacker and helping avert a potential disaster. The aircraft was subsequently diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, where the injured pilot received emergency treatment before being shifted to Abu Dhabi for further care.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Machchhar soon after the incident and praised his courage and presence of mind. His actions also drew appreciation from Indian officials and authorities in Israel (including PM Netanyahu) and the UAE.Machchhar underwent surgery and has been recovering in Abu Dhabi. The ministry of external affairs reported that his condition was improving.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rail disruption in Staffordshire due to overhead line fault
articles.summary: A fault with overhead wires near Penkridge is causing disruption between Stafford and Wolverhampton.
articles.body:
Rail passengers are being urged to check before they travel due to overhead line problems on the West Coast Main Line in Staffordshire.

Work was ongoing to fix a fault with the 25,000-volt wires which power trains near Penkridge, causing disruption between Stafford and Wolverhampton.

At 12:00 BST, National Rail confirmed that lines have reopened between Stafford and Birmingham New Street, but residual disruption can still be expected until 16:00 BST on Saturday.

Adam Checkley from Network Rail, said: "Our teams have now cleared the issue allowing the route to reopen, but with trains and their crew out of position, delays and cancellations will continue throughout the day."

Rail replacement buses are in place at Birmingham, Stafford and Wolverhampton.

Checkley added: "We're sorry to passengers impacted by the overhead line problems at Four Ashes near Penkridge.

"With disruption to train services likely throughout the day, I'd urge people to check National Rail Enquiries before they set off on their journey."

Ticket acceptance is in place on alternative routes including the East Coast Main Line, and Midland Main Line via Sheffield.

articles.title: Cornish art collection returns home for exhibition
articles.summary: The paintings have returned to Cornwall before embarking on a national tour.
articles.body:
Paintings depicting life in Cornwall's fishing and rural communities more than a century ago have gone on display.

The exhibition brings together 40 works from the acclaimed Bowerman Collection of Newlyn School art, a movement of artists who settled in west Cornwall in the late 19th Century.

The works have returned to Cornwall before embarking on a national tour and will be displayed at the Penlee House Gallery and Museum in Penzance until January.

Curator Alison Bevan said the work "captures the real lives and characters of this remote fishing community".

Bevan said the exhibition also highlighted artists who formed what she described as a second flowering of the colony at the turn of the 20th Century.

"With their more vibrant palette but equal passion for painting from life, this second generation re-energised Newlyn as a vibrant artistic hub, revelling in West Cornwall's sparkling light," she said.

The exhibition runs until 9 January before the collection begins a two-year tour of venues across England.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday warned that he would be compelled to consider an “Anshan Fast or Padyatra March” if those detained
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday warned that he would be compelled to consider an “Anshan Fast or Padyatra March” if those detained during protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar were not released by Sunday.In a video message posted on X, Wangchuk described the situation in the national capital as an “undeclared EMERGENCY” and expressed concern over the detention of several political leaders who had planned to participate in a protest demanding Kumar’s resignation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.“Yesterday when I posted a message appealing for unity & peace in today's protest I had never imagined that the biggest democracy in the world would be under an undeclared EMERGENCY. I was happy there were so many leaders to lead the movement, but I now learn that they have all been arrested. I hope those arrested will be released soon. I will be compelled to consider an Anshan Fast or Padyatra March if they are not released by tomorrow,” he said.Among those detained on Saturday were Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and All India Students' Association (AISA) leader Neha Bora. Delhi Police continued to take protesters into preventive custody after informing them that permission had not been granted for the gathering.Following his detention, Kejriwal posted a video on X alongside AAP leader Sanjay Singh, asserting that the protesters would not be intimidated.“We have been detained by the police. Sanjay Singh is here with me. The youth of the country has awakened. We are not going to be intimidated by Modi's tyranny. Now, Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign. People will not tolerate this stealing of votes anymore. You all should also come out of your homes and fight to save the country,” Kejriwal said.Bora also confirmed her detention and urged young people to continue the protest despite police action.“We have been detained. But it does not matter. To my fellow Gen Z: This is our 1942. Their jails can hold a few of us but not all of us. Wherever any of us is stopped today, we sit down right there and begin. Every corner becomes Jantar Mantar,” she wrote on X.Delhi Police sources said around 1,000 protesters had been detained across the national capital while attempting to march towards Jantar Mantar for the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led demonstration. A 31-year-old man has been held on suspicion of possessing an aggressive animal.

The force has not confirmed the breed of dog.

articles.title: 3 more govt employees held for Rs 9.24cr embezzlement; no. of arrests goes up to 9
articles.summary: Odisha Vigilance arrests 3 more govt staff in Rs 9.24 crore R&B fake bill scam; total arrests rise to 9 as probe tracks IFMS-linked money trail.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Vigilance officials on Saturday arrested three more persons in connection with the alleged embezzlement of over Rs 9.24 crore from the roads and buildings (R&B) department, taking the total number of arrests in the case to nine.The latest arrests include a senior accountant of the district treasury office in Bhubaneswar, Krushna Chandra Behera; a senior assistant currently posted in the R&B division in Puri, Biswanath Das; and Kumud Sahoo, a peon attached to R&B division-I here. All three were produced in the special vigilance court.According to investigators, the fraud involved preparation and clearance of fake bills in the names of retired employees, through which gratuity, leave salary and other benefits were illegally diverted to bank accounts linked to the accused and their associates. Earlier, six persons, including a section officer and a junior assistant — Banalata Mohanty and Bibhudatta Nayak — identified as the key conspirators, were arrested.The probe revealed that out of the Rs 9.24 crore fraud, the treasury official allegedly received Rs 3.9 lakh through 11 online transactions between March 2025 and July 2026 to facilitate passage of fraudulent bills without raising objections.The Vigilance inquiry also found that between financial years 2022-23 and 2025-26, Nayak and Mohanty, in conspiracy with others, generated fake sanction orders and fraudulent bills in the names of retired employees and against contingency funds.Investigators alleged that the forged bills were processed through the Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) using substituted bank account details, enabling the accused to siphon off govt money. While genuine beneficiaries were excluded, funds were routed to bank accounts belonging to relatives, acquaintances and associates of the accused.Altogether 77 bank accounts linked to 48 persons, including family members and associates of the accused, were reportedly used to receive the diverted funds. Portions of the money were later transferred back to the main accused or withdrawn in cash and handed over to them.Like the senior assistant, Sahoo also allegedly shared his wife’s bank account details, into which over Rs 11.25 lakh was credited as provisional gratuity. articles.title: Vedic vs Western Astrology: Why Your Navratri Horoscope Shows a Different Sign
articles.summary: You've been a Libra your whole life. Then an Indian friend reads your Navratri horoscope and calls you a Virgo.
articles.body: You've been a Libra your whole life. Then an Indian friend reads your Navratri horoscope and calls you a Virgo. Or a Kanya, which turns out to mean the same thing.Nobody made a mistake. You're looking at two different systems of astrology, built on two different maps of the sky. During Navratri season, when Vedic horoscopes flood social media, the difference becomes hard to miss.Two Zodiacs, One SkyWestern astrology uses the tropical zodiac. It's anchored to the seasons. The zodiac always begins at the spring equinox, the moment around March 20 when the Sun crosses the celestial equator. That point is called 0° Aries every single year.Vedic astrology, also called Jyotish, uses the sidereal zodiac. It's anchored to the actual stars. Signs line up with the constellations behind them.About two thousand years ago, these two zodiacs matched almost perfectly. Since then, they've slowly drifted apart.Blame the WobbleEarth wobbles on its axis, a bit like a spinning top slowing down. This wobble is called precession. It shifts the equinox point backwards against the stars by about one degree every 72 years.Add that up over centuries, and the gap between the two zodiacs today is roughly 24 degrees. This gap is called the ayanamsa.Since each sign spans 30 degrees, a 24-degree shift moves most people back one sign. If you were born in roughly the first three weeks of your Western sign, your Vedic Sun sign is probably the one before it.Navratri 2026 Shows the Gap ClearlyThis October is full of examples.·New Moon, October 10: Western astrology places it in Libra. Vedic charts put it in Virgo.·Venus retrograde, from October 3: Western astrologers have it starting in Scorpio. In Vedic terms, it's retrograde in Libra, its own sign.·Jupiter: It's in Leo in Western charts. Vedic charts show it in Cancer, where it's exalted, which is why Indian astrologers are so excited about this Navratri.·The Sun: It entered Western Libra around September 22. In Vedic astrology, it doesn't enter Libra until October 17, a day celebrated in India as Tula Sankranti.Same planets. Same moment. Different labels.Sun Sign or Moon Sign?There's a second reason Vedic horoscopes feel unfamiliar. They usually don't lead with your Sun sign at all.In the West, "What's your sign?" means where the Sun was when you were born. In India, the more common question is your Rashi, which is your Moon sign. The Moon moves quickly, changing signs every two and a half days, so it's seen as a better reflection of your mind and emotions.So when you read a Navratri Rashifal, it's almost always written for your Moon sign. You'll need your birth date, time and place to find it. Plenty of free online calculators can do this in under a minute. Make sure you pick the Lahiri ayanamsa setting, which is the standard in India.Which One Is Right?Neither system is "wrong." They simply ask different questions.Western astrology follows the seasons. It's rooted in the rhythm of light and dark across the year, which is why Aries season always begins with spring.Vedic astrology follows the stars themselves. It also comes with its own tools, like nakshatras, the 27 lunar mansions, and dashas, long planetary periods that map out phases of a person's life.Many people find both useful. A Western chart can feel great for personality and psychology. A Vedic chart is often used for timing, such as when to start a business or fix a wedding date.Try Both This NavratriLook up your Vedic Moon sign before October 11. Then read a Navratri Rashifal written for it, alongside your usual Western horoscope.You might find they say surprisingly similar things. Or you might find that one simply clicks more. Either way, you'll have a much better idea of why that Indian friend kept calling you a Kanya.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: ‘Their core characteristic is cowardice’: Rahul Gandhi targets PM Modi, RSS; backs youth protesting against CEC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday backed youth protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday backed youth protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Lok Sabha leader of the opposition said he had been fighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), the ideological mentor of the ruling BJP, for “over a decade now” and knew them “inside out, like the back of my hand."“The core characteristic of these people is cowardice. Narendra Modi, (Union home minister) Amit Shah, Gyanesh Kumar and (National Security Advisor) Ajit Doval are slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space,” Rahul Gandhi said in a video message on X.“Mr Modi, do whatever you want. Call out all the police. Arrest all the leaders. Arrest all the young people. Arrest us all,” he added.He further claimed to have “all the information we need,” an apparent reference to proof of what he describes as “vote chori” (vote theft) by the BJP in collusion with the Election Commission.“We are going to defend our Constitution. We are going to protect the voice of the Indian people. And we are going to ensure that what was done to India over the last 10-15 years will never, ever be done again,” the Raebareli MP further stated.“Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you. We are going to ensure that this regime and the people who have attacked our Constitution are defeated,” Rahul Gandhi asserted.His remarks came amid a protest led by the youth pressure group Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on Saturday.Delhi Police detained more than 3,000 protesters attempting to reach the site. Over 600 people with criminal records were also detained as a preventive measure. articles.title: Sidhu Moosewala returns to stage through 3D hologram show in Toronto
articles.summary: Sidhu Moosewala’s ‘Signed to God’ 3D hologram world tour launches in Toronto, featuring “295”; more shows set across Canada and US.
articles.body: Bathinda: Slain Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala returned to the stage through a 3D holographic performance in Toronto, Canada, on Friday night, as part of the launch of a world tour, ‘Signed to God’. His hit song 295, released in July 2021, was reintroduced in a new format during the show.The performance used holographic technology to recreate Moosewala on stage, complete with speech and audience interaction. The song has garnered 889 million views and 12 million likes on his YouTube channel, which has 31.5 million subscribers.Moosewala’s parents, Balkaur Singh and Charan Kaur, and his younger brother, Shubhdeep, born in March 2024, attended the opening show. Addressing the gathering, Balkaur Singh said the family had been fighting for justice for his son’s killing for more than four years.“To get justice, we need power, for which I am again fighting,” he said. He added that while attempts had been made to silence the singer, his voice continued to resonate. Seventeen songs have been released since his death, with another due soon, he said.Young Shubhdeep drew loud applause at the packed venue when he performed his father’s signature thapi gesture.The family and the singer’s team had been preparing for the tour for a long time. Five more shows are planned in the first phase, with performances scheduled in Vancouver and Calgary in Canada, and New York, Houston and Oakland in the US by Nov 6.Moosewala was shot dead on May 29, 2022, at Jawaharke village near Mansa while travelling in his black Thar with two friends.
